auth.cache_description: When API_KEY is set, every API request requires Authorization: Bearer <key>. Missing or invalid keys return HTTP 401 with Error 401. Protected responses use private, no-store; server-side result caching can still be used. Without API_KEY, the API remains public and single-lookup responses allow shared caching.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.description: Next Whois provides a simple REST API for WHOIS/RDAP lookups and OG images. Set the server environment variable API_KEY to require Bearer authentication. In the UI, use the API key button in the navigation bar; the key is stored locally in your browser.
docs.lookup_description: Query a domain, IP address, ASN or CIDR using RDAP first. If RDAP has no usable record or fails, fall back to WHOIS. Missing individual fields stay Unknown; the selected source’s raw response is included.
docs.lookup_query_desc: Domain name, IPv4/IPv6 address, ASN (e.g. AS13335), or CIDR range. Alias: q
docs.og_description: Generate a dynamic Open Graph image with WHOIS details. Internally queries /api/lookup and renders a card-style summary. Returns a PNG image.
docs.og_query_desc: Domain name, IP, ASN, or CIDR to look up and display. Alias: q
docs.rate_limiting_desc1: Successful WHOIS lookup responses are cached server-side (Redis) and served with
docs.rate_limiting_time: in the JSON body and report
docs.batch_description: Submit a small batch of queries. Results retain input order and duplicates; a failed item does not affect other items. Accepted batches return HTTP 200; inspect each item’s status.
docs.batch_queries_desc: Nonempty array of domain, IP, ASN or CIDR strings.
docs.batch_limits: Default maximum: 10 entries, counting duplicates. JSON body limit: 64 KiB. Requires Content-Type: application/json. Batch responses always use no-store.
docs.concurrency_description: Single and batch lookups share outgoing registration limits: 20 connections per process, 5 per external hostname by default. Discovery, redirects and referrals use the same queue. Each connection has a 5-second deadline; a lookup including queueing has a 30-second deadline.
docs.cache_description: Successful results are cached in memory for one hour by default, with optional Redis persistence. Errors are not cached. Concurrent requests for the same normalized query share one lookup; joining an in-flight lookup reports cached: false.
